findings.message: The final-pass fix (a proposal keeps its stored repo phases only while its row holds the same change folder and isn't withdrawn) has no test that drives the real write path. In the new tests, `storedPhasesFor` gets hand-made rows, and `desired()` gets a hand-made `{ repoPhases: storedPhasesFor(...) }`. No test pushes or syncs a reused key, or a withdrawn change coming back, through `pushSpecclaw` / `syncProposal` and then reads `meta.repoPhases` back. So the call on the locked row in `upsertSpecProposal` is unguarded: revert it to `before?.meta?.repoPhases` and every 096 test still passes. Fix: add a DB-backed table test over at least three cases (another folder takes the key on main; a withdrawn row's folder comes back; the same folder stays live) and check the stored `meta.repoPhases` each time.
findings.scenario: Revert services.ts:323 to `resolveRepoPhases(..., before?.meta?.repoPhases)`. FLT-971 is stored from `971-a` with `verify` recorded. A main push carries `971-b` (`971-a` is gone) with only a `proposal` time. The new folder's proposal then shows the old change's 'Verified in the repo' line, and every test in repo-sync-096.test.ts and repo-dates-094.test.ts still passes.

findings.message: The README's 096 sentence says a phase the repo reached stays recorded, but it leaves out the final pass's limit: stored phases are kept only while the row holds the same change folder (`source_ref`) and isn't withdrawn. A folder renamed on the default branch, which 091 allows, therefore starts again from its new read. The README should state this rule and its consequence for renames, so the code and the docs agree.
findings.scenario: 096-foo was verified on 18 Oct, then verify was re-run and failed (status no longer done). The folder is renamed to 096-foo-v2 on main. The push drops the stored `verify` entry, so the proposal's history loses 'Verified in the repo', while the README promises it stays.

findings.message: `repoBy` still has its own `@<sha>$` regex for the history line's 'read at …' text. 096 rounds 1–2 made `sync/sha.ts` (`READ` / `readParts`) the one `<ref>@<sha>` rule for every caller. This copy doesn't check the ref part, so a stored read that isn't `<ref>@<sha>` is still shown as one. It should shorten the sha through `readParts` and fall back to plain 'From the repo' when the source isn't a read.
findings.scenario: A phase stored with source 'the repo' (kept as stored, per round 1) displays as 'From the repo, read at the repo'. `isRead('the repo')` is false, so the shared rule would show plain 'From the repo'.

findings.message: `storedPhasesFor` treats any change of folder name as a different change (`row.source_ref === sourceRef`) and drops all stored phases. The README (091 AC-2, push.ts:107-108) says the default branch may rename a change, and its push then carries only the new folder. A rename is the same change, but under this rule it loses every phase it already reached, plus the read that first recorded each one. That breaks 096 AC-1 ('a phase the repo reached stays recorded'). The same rule runs in `desired()` (push.ts:121, import.ts:108) and in `upsertSpecProposal` (services.ts:323), so every path loses the history. Fix: tell a rename apart from a reuse of the number before dropping phases. For example, keep the stored phases when the row is live and the change on the default branch no longer has its old folder, and drop them only when the old folder is withdrawn, or when two folders share the number (that case is already a `duplicate`). Add a test for the rename case.
findings.scenario: FLT-096 is stored with source_ref '096-repo-sync' and repoPhases { proposal, verify (main@4f2c9a1) }. On main the folder is renamed to '096-repo-sync-follow-ups', and verify is re-run and fails, so state.json no longer marks verify done. The default-branch push sends dir '096-repo-sync-follow-ups' with phaseTimes { proposal }. `storedPhasesFor` returns undefined, so the stored meta.repoPhases becomes { proposal: { source: <this push> } }. The verify history line is lost and proposal's first read is re-attributed.
